patterns.title: Standardized Module Interfaces
patterns.summary: Preserve the connection contract between replaceable units so suitable alternatives can work without redesigning their neighbors.

identity_resolution.boundary: Segmentation chooses independently manageable units. Adapter translates an existing software mismatch, Bridge separates software variation dimensions, and Modular Upgrade Revenue concerns a business offering. This article specifies the physical, electrical, fluid, and semantic contract that approved replacement units preserve. Different implementations may share it; Common Parts instead reduces the assortment of actual components.

use_when: Replaceable units must substitute without redesigning surrounding equipment.
Multiple suppliers or product variants must preserve defined boundary behavior.
A mechanically mating replacement can still have incompatible ratings, supply conditions, or signal meaning.
goals: Permit internal implementation variation within a defined compatibility family
not_ideal_when: The supposed common interface erases consequential functional differences.
A universal envelope or protocol adds more burden than the compatibility family justifies.
No process exists for checking conformity or managing revisions.
example_user_queries: The replacement valve has the right bolt holes but does not fit between the pipes.
How can we change suppliers without redesigning the surrounding machine?
Our sensor connector fits but the displayed pressure is wrong.
What should a replaceable module's interface specification include?
Can different components be interchangeable without using the same part number?
A new sensor has the same current output but a different measurement range.
Which dimensions have to stay fixed when a valve is replaced?
How do we keep module revisions compatible with installed equipment?
We need to specify the connector, mounting face, power, and signal meaning together.
Does matching a flange size prove the replacement is suitable?
Should we preserve an interface or adapt each new component separately?
How can we verify that a new head works with our existing receiver?

related_patterns.title: Segmentation
related_patterns.relationship: Direct parent; chooses the manageable-unit boundary without guaranteeing interchangeability.

related_patterns.title: Common Parts
related_patterns.relationship: Different from this pattern: reduces actual component variety rather than preserving a common connection contract.

related_patterns.title: Reconfigurable Architecture
related_patterns.relationship: Can be enabled by stable connections; changes working arrangement, not just substitutability.

related_patterns.title: Adapter
related_patterns.relationship: Cross-verse software analogy: translates a mismatch; this pattern defines the intended stable physical-engineering boundary.

worked_examples.name: Reserved isolation-valve station
worked_examples.limits: Teaching values are not ASME dimensions or a buildable flange specification. Does not evaluate tolerances, gasket behavior, loads, pressure rating, or functional compliance.

worked_examples.name: Two approved pressure heads

contract.output: Sourced current with compatible receiver load

worked_examples.limits: Project-only connector and mounting sketch. Not an industry pinout, a TI device, or an IEEE 1451.4 implementation. Accuracy, dynamics, environment, and fault criteria require additional specified checks.

worked_examples.name: Mechanically mating but semantically incompatible head
worked_examples.limits: Linear mapping arithmetic on declared fixtures; not measured sensor error, fault detection, or device damage characterization. A valid electrical range does not establish compatible meaning.

graphics.decision: Three static original SVG figures and phone companions; no widget.
graphics.reason: The exploded station and heads expose the physical contract; the fixed 12 mA plot exposes the semantic mismatch. No necessary learning question requires a simulation.
graphics.style: Approved fixed-white editorial engineering style with regular Helvetica Neue, fine neutral lines, and restrained green.
graphics.provenance: Original schematic geometry and a calculated linear fixture. Not traced from standards, manufacturer drawings, or photographs.
